context: a letter from W. E. Darwin, which you are answering
exchanges:
I have looked at Chrysosplene, but cannot tell whether there are glands. it has hairs white, transparent, on leaves and stem; those on the stem have a hollow looking cup at the end of a red colour; the remainder of the hairs being silvery white, and transparent.

I send you a sketch by Camera Lucida of end of hair and cup.

I will send you some if there are glands.

I am your affect son | W E Darwin

I never saw such an organ as that which you draw; I shd. very much like to see a specimen.— Does the cup secrete any viscid matter? Please send the spec. in tin cannister or box with a little damp blotting paper. Botanists call all out of the way organs “glands” & no doubt they would call this a gland.—

Your affect | C. Darwin

I do not want Oxalis.

Are little insects ever caught in the cup??
